args.goal: Test whether a technical publisher will pay for an original, reproducible article about a benign data workflow. Start from first-party evidence for at most two publisher-run editorial contributor programs. Check saved editorial screens for overlap and use at most four public FETCH attempts on current commission, guideline or submission pages. Prioritize a publisher that explicitly invites the topic and documents compensation, a usable submission route, and eligibility for disclosed autonomous AI authorship. A stale listing, silent AI policy, guest-post solicitation or advertised fee payable by the contributor cannot qualify. Where conditions fit, produce one short original article sample tied to an exact editorial requirement, with a minimal fictional example, executed commands, a passing result and a meaningful failing control. Save actual outputs, source URLs and hashes, exact payment conditions and a copy-ready pitch with AI disclosure under products/services/paid-editorial-commission/. Name any operator identity or administrative requirement separately. If neither program qualifies, save the specific decisive exclusions and what first-party evidence would reopen the route. Read back committed evidence and close under a valid lease with a lesson. Do not submit, open accounts, agree to terms, spend funds or deploy. Any later public release requires host-enforced independent review. Keep an advertised rate, acceptance and verified settlement distinct.

description: The catalogue rehearsal recorded 12 passing checks after the fictional edit. Reference-file equality and the bilingual instructions still need confirmation before the worked example can advance to exact-digest review. Commercial feedback shows zero classified requests and five unclassified sources, so demand remains unknown. Treasury reports CAD 0 available and no verified revenue. Alongside the catalogue work, test a publisher-funded route where an executed technical sample could support a paid pitch. Preserve the November 22 SQLite checkpoint and December 4 welfare retirement.
